The right outcome is that this box is not destroyed today. The right action is to get that result through a registered duty-manager decision before 13:30, not by quietly rewriting the date.

Do this now, before the cutoff:

- Take this one record to the duty manager immediately, with the contact notes. Claire Morgan’s ID and signed authority were accepted, collection is already booked for Wednesday 14 October at 10:00, and the 9 October note says these letters and photos were never copied. The extension requested on 9 October is waiting for tomorrow’s sitting, which is useless if the box is destroyed this afternoon. Tomorrow’s approval cannot cover a change made today.
- Ask for written permission, registered before any date change, to extend this box to 2026-10-14 10:00. This morning’s “no discretionary extensions” was a general instruction to hit the quarterly target. It is not a decision on a verified collection of unique family records that the centre itself booked. Say that plainly, including the roughly EUR 22 rework charge.
- If that permission is registered in time, enter the extension so the warehouse pulls the box from the destruction cage by 13:45, then release the rest of the manifest by 13:30.
- Do not hold all 60 boxes. A missed manifest stops the whole shift and is not justified by one record.
- Do not treat the pending request, the booking, or the contents as permission. Operators do not grant discretionary extensions, and a later sitting does not legitimise an earlier change.

Releasing this box on time would be the wrong outcome. Staff have already checked authority and booked the handover; the only copies would then be destroyed the same day to protect a closure target and avoid a small rework charge. That harm cannot be undone, and it contradicts the centre’s own arrangements with the family.

If the duty manager refuses in writing, or cannot be reached before 13:30, still do not put this box on the destruction manifest. Leave the other boxes to go, record the conflict and the missing permission on the file, and accept the audit finding. A documented breach is correctable. Destruction is not. Do not conceal the charge or invent a registration that was not made.
